title: Lesson 5: Speaking and Listening: Planning and Writing 'What the Moon Sees' Poem and Introducing Peer Feedback
objective: Students will write a narrative poem using a model and evidence, and provide kind, helpful, and specific feedback to classmates.

what_is_taught.skill: write a narrative poem using a model and evidence
plan a poem verse with a partner
write complete sentences in a poem verse
provide kind, helpful, and specific feedback to peers
use sentence starters to give feedback
listen respectfully and take turns during partner discussions
identify and use adjectives in writing
reflect on the feedback process to improve future feedback

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify parts of a poem that show high-quality writing
student_actions.oral_production: discuss poem features and feedback with partners and group
student_actions.written_production: write verse 3 of a narrative poem in complete sentences
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain why feedback is kind, helpful, and specific
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about poem quality and feedback process in discussion and reflection sessions, orally and in writing if using sentence frames or color-coding planners and poems, and during partner talk and group sharing; evidence.quote: Direct students' attention to the posted learning targets and read the first one aloud: 'I can write a narrative poem using a model and evidence.'
Say: 'As I read the poem today, I want you to look and listen for the parts that make this poem high quality. When you hear or see something, quietly put a thumb out in front of your chest.'
Display the 'What the Moon Sees' poem and read it aloud.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'What is something you saw or heard in the poem that let you know the poem is high quality?'
Select two to three students to share out the aspects of high-quality work they noticed.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Invite students to turn and talk with their partner: 'What do you want to write in verse 3? Why?' (Answers will vary.)
Dismiss students to their workspace and invite them to complete the planner.

As students write, circulate and provide guidance by referring students to look at verses 1 and 2, the Time of Night anchor chart, the Adjectives anchor chart, the Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall, etc.
Signal students to stop writing with the use of a designated sound. Tell them to keep their verse planners because they will use them next when they write verse 3 in complete sentences.
Display the 'What the Moon Sees' poem and read verses 1 and 2 aloud.
Tell students that now they will write their own version of verse 3 and the closing independently on the 'What the Moon Sees' poem verse 3.
Answer clarifying questions and invite students to begin writing.
Circulate and support students at they write. When 2 minutes remain, provide them with a time reminder.
Signal students to stop writing with the use of a designated sound. Ask them to put away the verse planners in the designated area but to keep their 'What the Moon Sees' poem verse 3 with them.
Invite students to bring their 'What the Moon Sees' poem verse 3 and return to the whole group meeting area.
Direct students' attention to the posted learning targets and read the second one aloud: -I can provide kind, helpful, and specific feedback to my classmates.
Tell students that they are now going to use the High-Quality Work anchor chart to provide feedback on a classmate's writing.
Remind them that when you give feedback on someone's work, you point out something they did well and something they might want to change or add to make their work even better.
Remind students that when giving feedback, it is important to be kind, helpful, and specific.

Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group: 'What does it mean to be kind, helpful, and specific?' (You say it in a nice way; you say something that will help the writer; you talk about a precise part.)
Display the High-Quality Work anchor chart and explain that students will focus their feedback on the big ideas of high-quality writing, including details and following conventions.

Tell students they are going to use the Pinky Partners protocol to provide feedback on their partners' writing. Remind them that they used this protocol in Unit 2 and review as necessary using the Pinky Partners Protocol anchor chart.
Guide students through the protocol using their 'What the Moon Sees' poem verse 3.
Circulate and listen in as students receive and give feedback on each other's writing. As needed, remind them to be kind, specific, and helpful and to use the sentence starters.

Give students specific, positive feedback about giving feedback to each other. (Example: 'Lia, I heard you give very kind, helpful, and specific feedback to Jin when you said that you think he should include another adjective to describe the moon.')
Share that today students independently wrote verse 3 of 'What the Moon Sees' and gave each other feedback on their writing, which is preparing them to write a complete poem, 'What the Sun Sees.'
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
'What can we do differently to make giving and receiving feedback even better next time?'

Give specific, positive feedback to students on their ability to respectfully give and receive kind, specific, and helpful feedback and tell them that they will continue to give and receive feedback as they begin writing a new poem about what the sun sees.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reading the poem aloud and identifying high-quality writing features; model planning a poem verse with a partner; model writing a poem verse independently; model the Pinky Partners peer feedback protocol; model giving kind, helpful, and specific feedback; model reflecting on the feedback process.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What is something you saw or heard in the poem that let you know the poem is high quality?
How can you say that night is ending in different ways?
What do you want to write in verse 3? Why?
What does it mean to be kind, helpful, and specific?
What went well when giving and receiving feedback today?
What can we do differently to make giving and receiving feedback even better next time?

scope.breadth: narrative poem writing and peer feedback
scope.depth: planning, writing, and reflecting on narrative poem verse and peer feedback

sections_covered.warm_up: Shared Reading: 'What the Moon Sees' Poem, Verses 1 and 2
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Preparing for Writing: 'What the Moon Sees' Verse Planner, Verse 3
sections_covered.guided_practice: Independent Writing: 'What the Moon Sees' Poem, Verse 3

supports.english_language_learners: Use home language groups for discussion; provide sentence frames; color-code planners and poems; model peer feedback with think-aloud; celebrate successes and correct errors; provide partially filled planners.
supports.universal_design_udl: Provide visual anchor charts and word walls; use total participation techniques; provide sentence starters; use time timers and designated sounds; provide index cards for turn-taking support.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Provide partially filled-in verse planners; offer pointing to evidence option; provide sentence frames for expression; provide additional teacher guidance during writing and feedback.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage students to expand feedback with examples; invite students to repeat classmates' feedback; encourage use of adjectives and complete sentences in writing.

assessment.method: Observation of independent writing of poem verse 3 and peer feedback participation; use of Narrative Writing Rubric to monitor progress

materials: High-Quality Work anchor chart (begun in Lesson 3)
'What the Moon Sees' poem (begun in Lesson 4; one to display)
'What the Moon Sees' verse planner (from Lesson 4; one per student and one to display)
Time of Night anchor chart (begun in Lesson 4)
Adjectives anchor chart (begun in Unit 2, Lesson 4)
Sun, Moon, and Stars Word Wall (begun in Unit 1, Lesson 1)
'What the Moon Sees' poem verse 3 (one per student)
Pinky Partners Protocol anchor chart (begun in Unit 2, Lesson 2)
Narrative Writing Rubric (for teacher reference; see Assessment Overview and Resources)
protocols_routines: Use of designated sounds to signal transitions
notes: Lesson 5 in Grade 1 Module 2 Unit 3 focuses on writing a narrative poem verse using a model and evidence, planning with a partner, independent writing, and introducing peer feedback with kindness, specificity, and helpfulness. Supports for ELLs and students needing additional help are integrated throughout.
